How to Invest in Alachua County, Florida Tax Deed Sales

If you’re an investor looking for real property deals in Florida, Alachua County’s tax sales are worth checking out.
Here’s a simple breakdown of how it works, what you need to know, and why this area could be a smart move for your money.

Understanding Alachua County’s Tax Sale Process

When a property owner doesn’t pay their property taxes by March 31, Alachua County steps in.
The tax sale process happens in two parts:

1. Tax Certificate Sales

  • Held annually, usually by June 1.
  • Online auction through LienHub (formerly RealAuction).
  • Investors bid by offering the lowest interest rate they are willing to accept (starting at 18%).
  • If the property owner pays the taxes back, you get your money plus interest.
  • If unpaid for 2 years, you can apply for a Tax Deed Sale.

2. Tax Deed Sales

  • After applying, the property is sold at a public auction through RealTDM.
  • Opening bid includes unpaid taxes, fees, and sale costs.
  • Highest bidder wins the property.
  • Full payment must be made within 24 hours of winning.

Why You Should Consider Alachua County for Tax Sale Investing

  • University of Florida drives rental demand in Gainesville.
  • Strong rental market because of students, hospitals, and tech growth.
  • Growing tech hub with research centers and startups.
  • Affordable compared to big cities like Miami or Orlando.
  • Outdoor attractions like Paynes Prairie and Ichetucknee Springs boost property values.

This mix means stable rental incomes, increasing property values, and great opportunities for tax deed investors.

Pro Tips for First-Time Investors

  • Do Your Research
    Look up every property for issues like liens, zoning problems, or physical damage.
  • Understand the Terms
    Every auction has clear payment deadlines. Miss it, and you lose the property and your deposit.
  • Stick to a Budget
    Don’t get carried away with bidding wars. Set a hard limit before you start.
  • Know About Surplus Funds
    If the property sells for more than owed, the extra money doesn’t go to you—it may go back to the previous owner.

FAQs About Alachua County Tax Sales

Q: Can anyone buy tax liens or deeds?
Yes. You don’t have to live in Florida to participate.

Q: Can I inspect the property before buying?
You can drive by, but you usually cannot enter. Properties are sold as-is.

Q: What happens if the owner pays the taxes?
If you hold the lien, you get back your investment plus interest.

Q: How do I apply for a tax deed?
After two years of holding a certificate without payment, you can start a deed application through the Clerk’s Office.

Q: Is it possible to lose money?
Yes. If you don’t research properly, you could buy a property with hidden liens or serious damage.
